program_educational_objectives.description: Prepare students to apply design principles and techniques to create innovative, functional, and sustainable architectural solutions that respond to the social, cultural, economic, and environmental context.
Equip students to work collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams, respecting diverse perspectives and engaging in constructive dialogue to address complex architectural problems.

Infuse a strong analytical foundation with the ability to conduct research, use evidence-based practices to inform design decisions, and continuously learn and adapt to emerging trends and challenges.
Train students to demonstrate a strong work ethic, integrity, and ethical responsibility towards society and environment in their professional practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Architectural Knowledge
programme_outcomes.description: Apply knowledge of design development, building technology, structural systems, environmental studies, humanities and management to develop architectural design solutions.

programme_outcomes.title: Problem analysis
programme_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, research and analyse complex architectural problems using cultural, historical and theoretical design discourses to reach substantiated inferences.

programme_outcomes.title: Design/development of solutions
programme_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex architectural problems meeting specified needs with appropriate consideration for cultural, societal, environmental, economic and aesthetic considerations.

programme_outcomes.title: Investigation of complex problems
programme_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge and methods, including design of experiments, data analysis and synthesis to arrive at rational and valid conclusions.

programme_outcomes.title: Modern tool usage
programme_outcomes.description: Apply traditional and contemporary design tools and techniques to formulate and communicate creative and innovative architectural design solutions.

programme_outcomes.title: Architect and the society
programme_outcomes.description: Apply reasoning supplemented by contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues relevant to the profession.

programme_outcomes.title: Environment and sustainability
programme_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of architectural solutions in societal and environmental contexts and demonstrate the need for sustainable development.

programme_outcomes.title: Ethics
programme_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commitment to professional ethics, responsibilities and norms of professional practice in Architecture.

programme_outcomes.title: Individual and team work
programme_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual, member or leader in diverse groups and multidisciplinary settings.

programme_outcomes.title: Communication
programme_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on architectural design solutions with the community and society, including documentation, presentations and instructions.

programme_outcomes.title: Project management and finance
programme_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge of project management and finance principles and apply them to manage projects in multidisciplinary environments.

programme_outcomes.title: Life-long learning
programme_outcomes.description: Recognise the need and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the context of rapid changes in technology.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Fine art skill
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Grasp fine arts (local, regional, national and international) as an influence on the quality of architectural design.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Legal Knowledge
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Knowledge of local by-laws, national and international codes and regulations related to the architectural profession.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Quantitative/Analytical skill
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Capable of quantifying and analysing complex building systems and performance.

programme_specific_outcomes.title: Entrepreneurial skill
programme_specific_outcomes.description: Enable establishing an independent practice, organising and managing an office while remaining accountable to society.

institute_core.title: Applied Mathematics
course_outcomes: CO1: Appreciate the role of differentiation and integration in architectural parameters like area and volume.
CO2: Associate the fundamental structure of 2D plane and 3D space with properties of different structures.
CO3: Represent lines, planes and 3D objects using different coordinate systems.
CO4: Comprehend various probability distributions.
CO5: Apply sampling and testing methods for different kinds of studies.
CO6: Perform testing of hypothesis and tests for goodness of fit.
topics: Basic Calculus: applications of differentiation, definite integrals, volumes by cross sections, solids of revolution, arc length, surface area
Double and triple integrals, their applications
Geometry: conic sections, coordinate systems (Cartesian, Polar, Spherical, Cylindrical), vectors, lines and planes in space
Curves in space, curvature, velocity and acceleration
Probability distributions: random variables, mean, variance, MGF, Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Normal, Uniform
Statistics: sampling distributions, point and interval estimation, hypothesis tests, chi-square test, contingency tables
references: G. B. Thomas & R. L. Finney, Calculus and Analytical Geometry, Addison-Wesley, 1998
R. A. Johnson, Miller and Freund's Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 8th Edn., PHI, 2011
S. M. Ross, Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 5th Edn., Elsevier, 2014

institute_core.title: Workshop
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify appropriate tools, materials and techniques used in different trades.
CO2: Explore the value of physical models as an integral part of a design process.
CO3: Gain knowledge about effective communication of design ideas through 3D visualisation and modelling.
CO4: Be imaginative and innovative in representational approaches using physical and digital fabrication skills.
CO5: Apply skills of using different media and scales creatively in architectural model making.
CO6: Demonstrate understanding of aesthetics and structural stability in building design models.
topics: Carpentry: tools, processes, marking, cutting, planning, simple models and joints
Sheet metal: tools, gauge selection, types of joints
Foundry: tools, sand preparation, moulding, casting demonstration
Electrical wiring: tools, wiring systems, lamp wiring, ELCB and MCB selection
Plumbing: PVC pipes, accessories, fittings
Architectural model making: need, scale, block and detailed models, tools, materials, 3D printing, CNC machines
references: N. Burbank, House Carpentry Simplified, McGraw Hill, 1986
K. B. Raina & S. K. Bhattacharya, Electrical Design Estimating and Costing, New Age International, 2005
D. Nick, Architectural Model Making, Laurence King, 2010

institute_core.title: Professional Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Distinguish the role and purpose of communication at the workplace and for academic purposes.
CO2: Decide strategies and modes for effective communication in a dynamic workplace.
CO3: Combine multiple approaches for successful and ethical information exchange.
CO4: Estimate best communication practices to assist productivity and congeniality.
topics: Listening and reading comprehension: introductions, feedback, public speaking
Vocabulary development, critical reading, text structures
Effective writing: note-making, paragraph writing, official letters, emails, abstract writing
Communication theory, verbal/nonverbal communication, group discussions, presentations, digital communication etiquette
references: N. Bhatnagar, Communicative English for Engineers and Professionals, Dorling Kindersley, 2010
B. A. Garner, HBR Guide to Better Business Writing, Harvard Business Review Press, 2012
S. Kumar & P. Lata, Communication Skills, Oxford University Press, 2015

institute_core.title: Professional Practice and Ethics
institute_core.description: Covers professional practice, legal frameworks, and ethical responsibilities of architects in professional settings.

programme_core.title: Ergonomics
course_outcomes: CO1: Comprehend environmental factors and human behavioural aspects in a design process.
CO2: Assess standards and principles of accessibility in universal design.
CO3: Demonstrate knowledge of relevant design standards and their application in architecture.
CO4: Analyze and design any space for ease of use and comfort.
CO5: Apply anthropometry and rational thinking while designing for different building types.
CO6: Review the built environment for universal access and suggest improvement measures.
topics: Human Factors: introduction to ergonomics, physical/physiological/psychological aspects, gross anatomy, posture, static and dynamic anthropometry, biomechanics
Environmental Factors: thermal, illumination, noise, vibration conditioning; occupational hazards; visual and postural stress
Design Requirements: built environment for differently abled, ramp/toilet/corridor design, wheelchair access, design for visually challenged
Design Standards: residential, institutional, cultural, health, public, commercial, transportation, recreational building types
references: A. R. Tilley, Henry Dreyfuss Associates, The Measure of Man & Woman, Whitney Library of Design, 2002
J. De Chiara & J. H. Callender, Time-saver Standards for Building Types, McGraw-Hill, 1983
J. E. Harrigan, Human Factors Research: Methods and Applications for Architects and Interior Designers, Elsevier, 2014

programme_core.title: Theory of Design
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify theoretical grounds in design thinking.
CO2: Analyze the design process in various ways.
CO3: Apply functional concepts of design.
CO4: Critique aesthetical aspects of design.
CO5: Develop design concepts based on thorough understanding.
CO6: Demonstrate theoretical approaches in the design process and decision-making.
topics: Perception of Design: affordance, anthropomorphic form, colour, figure-ground relationship, layering, legibility, proximity, 3D projection
Functionality of Design: accessibility, usability, confirmation, control, cost-benefit, mental model, wayfinding
Aesthetics of Design: attractive bias, cognitive dissonance, golden ratio, proportional density, symmetry, storytelling
Design Decision Making: convergence, design by committee, expectation effect, factor of safety, iteration, prototyping, redundancy
references: W. Lidwell, K. Holden & J. Butler, Universal Principles of Design, Rockport, 2010
M. Macnab, Design by Nature, New Riders, 2011
W. Wong, Principles of Form and Design, Wiley, 1993

programme_core.title: Architectural Graphics
course_outcomes: CO1: Construct lines for different purposes, do lettering and dimensioning.
CO2: Apply orthographic projection to represent lines, planes, solids and development of surfaces.
CO3: Present 3D objects using orthographic and axonometric projections.
CO4: Create different types of perspective projections of solids, buildings and interiors.
CO5: Prepare different types of presentation drawings with or without sciography.
topics: Conventions, techniques and standards: types of lines, lettering, dimensioning, BIS code, basic geometric constructions (1 drawing exercise)
Orthographic projections: first and third angle projections, projection of points, lines, planes and solids, auxiliary projections, sections, surface development (5 exercises)
Pictorial projections: axonometric and isometric projections, perspective views of solids, buildings and interiors (5 exercises)
Presentation drawings and sciography: shades and shadows, application on pictorial views (2 exercises)
references: F. D. Ching, Architectural Graphics, Wiley, 2003
K. C. John & P. I. Varghese, Engineering Graphics, Jet Publications, 2004
S. Mulik, Perspectives and Sciography, Allied Publishers, 1999

programme_core.title: Introduction to Design - I
course_outcomes: CO1: Enhance use of freehand drawing and lettering for design communication.
CO2: Understand and analyse drawing conventions.
CO3: Interpret and apply elements and principles of design.
CO4: Interpret, evaluate and apply anthropometrics in design.
CO5: Represent 3D objects with plans, elevations, sections and views.
CO6: Apply the process of design and create a simple architectural form.
topics: Design Process: study of an everyday object, 2D representation, fitness for purpose, materials, durability, environmental considerations, redesign
Principles of Design: emphasis, balance, contrast, repetition, proportion, movement, figure/ground, rhythm, pattern, hierarchy, unity, harmony
Anthropometry: static and functional anthropometry, Indian standards, percentile concepts, furniture documentation and analysis
Design and Representation: design generation, refinement, 3D studies, schematic development, study models, architectural drawings, rendering
references: F. D. Ching, Architecture: Form, Space, and Order, Wiley, 2023
E. Neufert & P. Neufert, Architects' Data, Wiley, 2012
W. Lidwell, K. Holden & J. Butler, Universal Principles of Design, Rockport, 2010

programme_core.title: Visual Art Studio
course_outcomes: CO1: State design principles within different visual compositions.
CO2: Create 2D compositions with appropriate media.
CO3: Create 3D compositions in various media.
CO4: Choose suitable materials for 2D and 3D compositions.
CO5: Critique visual relationships of different compositions.
CO6: Distinguish between different genres of applied art.
topics: Fundamentals: elements and principles of design, Gestalt principles, colour theory, exploration of media (pencil, ink, crayon, pastels, watercolours)
Art: 2D visual properties, colour theory application, rendering techniques, perspective views, Indian aesthetics
Sculpture: art in 3D, form, texture, mass and volume, casting, modelling, additive/subtractive techniques, clay, plaster, paper, wire
Applied Art: architecture, interior design, graphics, fashion design; art appreciation, aesthetics, perception, symbolism
references: F. D. Ching, Architectural Graphics, Wiley, 2003
F. D. Ching, Form, Space and Order, Wiley, 2007
V. S. Parmer, Design Fundamentals in Architecture, Somaiya Publications, 2010

programme_core.title: Applied Mechanics
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe fundamentals of mechanics and equivalent force systems.
CO2: Classify statically determinate and indeterminate structures.
CO3: Analyse statically determinate structures including trusses.
CO4: Compute shear force and bending moment for various loading conditions.
CO5: Compute frictional forces acting on a body.
CO6: Determine sectional properties for various sections.
topics: Fundamentals: basic dimensions and units, vector and scalar quantities, laws of mechanics, moment of a force, couples
Equivalent force systems: translation of force, resultant of force systems, distributed force systems
Equations of equilibrium: free body diagrams, Lami's theorem, static indeterminacy
Structural mechanics: trusses, method of joints and sections
Section forces in beams: types of beams, shear force and bending moment diagrams
Friction: Coulomb friction laws; Properties of surfaces: centroid, moment of inertia, polar moment, principal axes
references: I. H. Shames & G. K. M. Rao, Engineering Mechanics, Pearson, 2005
F. P. Beer & E. R. Johnston, Vector Mechanics for Engineers — Statics, McGraw Hill, 2013
J. L. Meriam & L. G. Kraige, Engineering Mechanics — Statics, 6th Edn., Wiley, 2010

programme_core.title: Introduction to Building Materials and Systems
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify the various building materials and systems present in a building.
CO2: Comprehend characteristics, properties and applications of various building materials.
CO3: Differentiate between structural and non-structural building systems.
CO4: Interpret the various building system functioning in a building.
CO5: Gain understanding of construction techniques related to building materials.
CO6: Suggest appropriate materials and systems for various spaces in buildings.
topics: Building materials: bricks, tiles, stones, sand, cement, mortars, concrete — types, properties, standards
Metals: ferrous metals (cast iron, wrought iron, steel), non-ferrous metals (aluminium, zinc, copper), corrosion prevention
Structural systems: evolution, building elements, components viewed through typical section
Non-structural systems: enclosure and protection, mechanical systems, transportation systems
references: S. C. Rangwala, Building Construction, 34th Edn., Charotar, 2022
E. A. Allen, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Wiley, 2009
F. Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Wiley, 2008

programme_core.title: Cultural Studies
course_outcomes: CO1: Acquire fundamental understanding of culture and its key elements.
CO2: Comprehend the impact of cultural beliefs on the built environment.
CO3: Recognise architecture as a reflection of cultural values and beliefs.
CO4: Appreciate diverse Traditional Knowledge Systems.
CO5: Grasp principles of designing culturally sensitive architecture.
CO6: Analyze cultural influences on the built environment and architectural design.
topics: Introduction to Cultural Studies: definition, components, anthropological/sociological/semiotic perspectives
Cultural influences on society: culture-society relationship, faith, power/patronage, commerce in early and indigenous societies
Cultural influences on built environment: cosmological models, geocultural regions, traditional knowledge systems, Indian knowledge systems
Cultural sensitivity in design: promoting cultural diversity, avoiding cultural appropriation, contemporary examples
references: A. Rapoport, House Form & Culture, Prentice Hall, 1969
Kostof, Spiro, A History of Architecture: Settings and Rituals, Oxford University Press, 2010
L. M. Roth & A. C. R. Clark, Understanding Architecture: Its Elements, History, and Meaning, Routledge, 2018

programme_core.title: Introduction to Design - II
course_outcomes: CO1: Analysis of precedents to arrive at programmatic requirements and make design decisions.
CO2: Understand and apply human scale in design.
CO3: Analyse and apply site and contextual determinants of architecture.
CO4: Prioritise design choices from firmness, commodity and delight.
CO5: Understand and apply design process informed by behavioural needs.
CO6: Efficiently communicate design ideation, development and presentation for multifunctional spaces.
topics: Use of precedents: elements of architecture through the immediate environment, human scale, programmatic requirements from case studies
Determinants of architecture: context, stakeholders, climate, site characteristics, behavioural needs
Weighing design choices: priorities of firmness, commodity and delight; spatial organisation, circulation, form and space
Multi-functional space design: planes, enclosure, play of light, articulation, floors, walls, roofs, fenestration, design communication
references: F. D. Ching, Architecture: Form, Space, and Order, Wiley, 2023
F. D. Ching, Architectural Graphics, Wiley, 2015
E. Neufert & P. Neufert, Architects' Data, Wiley, 2012

programme_core.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify and differentiate computer graphics formats, techniques and tools.
CO2: Create raster and vector-based graphics and page layouts for design communication.
CO3: Create 2D CAD drawings.
CO4: Create 3D models.
topics: Essentials of computer graphics: historical development, raster/vector representation, colour models (RGB, CMYK), image formats, printing, hardware
Raster image manipulation: brushes, layers, selection tools, curves, filters (Gimp/Photoshop)
Vector image manipulation: shapes, paths, pen tool, gradients, layers (Inkscape/Illustrator)
Page layout: document setup, text styles, image manipulation, brochures, multi-page reports (Scribus/InDesign)
2D CAD: user interface, drawing commands, modification tools, layers, annotation, plotting, sheet layouts (AutoCAD/IIA CAD)
3D graphics: coordinate systems, polygon/spline/blobby modelling, rendering (scanline, ray tracing, AI-assisted), animation basics (Blender/Sketchup)
references: J. J. McConnell, Computer Graphics Theory into Practice, National Book Traders, 2006
G. Omura & B. C. Benton, Mastering AutoCAD 2018, Sybex/Wiley, 2017
Autodesk User Manual for CAD

programme_core.title: Surveying and Levelling
course_outcomes: CO1: Understand principles of surveying.
CO2: Carry out distance measurements using different survey equipment.
CO3: Adopt suitable survey technique and select equipment based on required accuracy.
CO4: Carry out profiling and grid levelling for contour maps and earthworks computations.
CO5: Analyse and synthesise survey data from field notes.
CO6: Carry out field surveys for location, design and construction of buildings, working effectively in a team.
topics: Surveying basics: plane and geodetic surveying, types of errors
Distance measurement: tape, tacheometry, EDM; systematic errors and corrections
Vertical control: levelling, height of collimation, rise and fall methods, differential and reciprocal levelling, contouring
Angle and direction measurement: bearings, azimuths, magnetic compass, theodolite, total station, traversing
Tacheometric surveying: stadia method, constants, tangential tacheometry
Computation of areas and volumes: traverse, cross sections, earthworks
lab_topics: Measurement of horizontal and vertical angles using Micro-optic Theodolite
Contour surveying using Total Station and QGIS
references: J. Anderson & E. Mikhail, Surveying: Theory and Practice, McGraw Hill, 7th Edn., 2017
R. Subramanian, Surveying and Levelling, Oxford University Press, 2nd Edn., 2012
B. C. Punmia, A. K. Jain & A. K. Jain, Surveying Vol-I, Laxmi Publications, 17th Edn., 2016

programme_core.title: Material Testing Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify the type of test depending on the material and property to be tested.
CO2: Carry out tests as per standard procedures.
CO3: Conduct standard tests on different building materials.
CO4: Determine properties of concrete and aggregate.
CO5: Determine properties of mild steel and timber.
CO6: Carry out construction of brick masonry and arches.
lab_topics: Tests on aggregate: grain size distribution, specific gravity, density, voids, bulking, aggregate crushing value, aggregate impact value
Tests on cement: fineness, normal consistency, setting time, compressive strength
Test on timber beam — bending test
Tests on tiles: dimension, transverse strength, water absorption, crazing
Tests on bricks: crushing strength, water absorption, efflorescence
Workability tests for fresh concrete and compressive strength of hardened concrete
Hands-on: bar bending for lintels and beams
references: A. M. Neville, Properties of Concrete, Prentice Hall, 2011
M. S. Shetty, Concrete Technology, S Chand, 2006
Relevant BIS Standards

programme_core.title: History of Architecture I
programme_core.description: Study of architectural history from ancient civilisations to medieval periods, examining the cultural, social, and technological contexts of architecture across regions.

programme_core.title: Site Planning and Building Regulations
programme_core.description: Principles of site planning and analysis, local and national building regulations, zoning, FAR, setbacks, and statutory requirements for architectural design.

programme_core.title: Theory of Structures I
programme_core.description: Analysis of statically determinate structures; stress and strain; bending of beams; deflection of beams; column behaviour.

programme_core.title: Building Climatology and Solar Architecture
programme_core.description: Climate and architecture; solar geometry; passive cooling and heating strategies; bioclimatic design; climate-responsive architectural design.

programme_core.title: Building Construction and Materials I
programme_core.description: Foundations, masonry construction, flooring, roofing, and building elements using traditional and modern materials.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour III
programme_core.description: Design studio focusing on residential or community buildings. Includes field tour to study built examples and site context.

programme_core.title: History of Architecture II
programme_core.description: Continuation of architectural history: Renaissance to Modern movement, regional architecture, and critical analysis of historical styles.

programme_core.title: Theory of Structures II
programme_core.description: Analysis of statically indeterminate structures; moment distribution method; introduction to space frames and arches.

programme_core.title: Building Services I (Water Supply, Sanitation and Air-conditioning)
programme_core.description: Water supply systems, sanitation and drainage, plumbing design, HVAC systems, and air-conditioning principles for buildings.

programme_core.title: Building Construction and Materials II
programme_core.description: Advanced construction techniques: RCC framed structures, formwork, waterproofing, doors, windows, and finishing.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour IV
programme_core.description: Design studio for institutional or public buildings with increased complexity. Field tour to study relevant building typologies.

programme_core.title: Structural Design I
programme_core.description: Limit state design of RC elements: beams, columns, slabs, and footings; IS code-based design.

programme_core.title: Contemporary Architecture
programme_core.description: Post-modern, deconstructivist, high-tech, and contemporary architectural movements; case study analysis of significant built works.

programme_core.title: Building Services II (Acoustics and Illumination)
programme_core.description: Principles of architectural acoustics, noise control, room acoustics design; natural and artificial illumination, daylighting strategies and lighting design.

programme_core.title: Building Construction and Materials III
programme_core.description: Steel and composite structures, prefabrication, industrial building construction, curtain walls, cladding, and special construction systems.

programme_core.title: Landscape Architecture Studio
programme_core.description: Principles of landscape design; site analysis; planting design; hardscape elements; integration of landscape with building design.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour V
programme_core.description: Design studio for complex multi-use or cultural buildings. Field tour for in-depth study of precedents.

programme_core.title: Estimation, Costing, and Specifications
programme_core.description: Methods of estimation, rate analysis, specifications writing, tendering procedures, and project costing in architectural practice.

programme_core.title: Structural Design II
programme_core.description: Advanced structural design: retaining walls, staircases, pre-stressed concrete, and introduction to special structures.

programme_core.title: Building Construction and Materials IV
programme_core.description: High-performance building envelopes, sustainable materials, renovation techniques, and innovative construction detailing.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour VI
programme_core.description: Design studio for large-scale or urban-context buildings integrating structural, services and landscape considerations.

programme_core.title: Building Systems and Science Lab
programme_core.description: Experimental and analytical study of building environmental systems: thermal comfort measurements, acoustic tests, daylighting assessments, and energy analysis tools.

programme_core.title: Urban Design
programme_core.description: Principles of urban design; public space, streetscape, and urban form analysis; urban morphology; case studies of successful urban districts.

programme_core.title: Interior Design
programme_core.description: Principles of interior design, space planning, material and furniture selection, lighting design, and preparation of interior design drawings.

programme_core.title: Working Drawing
programme_core.description: Preparation of complete working drawing sets including plans, sections, elevations, construction details, schedules, and specifications.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour VII
programme_core.description: Advanced design studio exploring complex urban or institutional projects. Field tour to study contemporary built work.

programme_core.title: Research Seminar
programme_core.description: Students identify a research theme, conduct literature review, and present findings as a seminar paper, preparing for thesis work.

programme_core.title: Architectural Design and Field Tour VIII
programme_core.description: Final pre-thesis design studio exploring a comprehensive architectural project integrating all learnings.

programme_core.title: Parametric Design/Simulation Lab
programme_core.description: Introduction to parametric and computational design tools; building performance simulation; generative design workflows.

programme_core.title: Office Training
programme_core.description: Practical training in an architectural firm, government body, or construction organisation. Duration includes the summer vacation preceding the Monsoon Semester. Per-week hours based on the host organisation's policy.

programme_core.title: Construction Site Study and Innovative Details Documentation
programme_core.description: Field documentation of an active construction site; study of innovative construction details; preparation of a detailed report.

programme_core.title: Critical Appraisal of Buildings
programme_core.description: Critical evaluation of significant buildings through site visits and analysis using architectural, cultural, and technical criteria.

programme_core.title: Thesis
programme_core.description: The culminating design project of the B.Arch. programme. Students develop an independently conceived architectural design project from initial research through final design, supported by a faculty thesis guide.
